skill.displayName: Work Productivity Humanizer Remove Workflow Helper

llm.summary: This is a documentation-only workflow helper with overly broad activation language, but it does not contain code, persistence, credential access, external execution, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The workflow explicitly prefers local-hardware-friendly scripts, templates, checklists, and CPU-safe workflows, which is proportionate to the documented purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown documentation and a small YAML agent metadata file only; no executable files, dependency installation, remote payload retrieval, or install scripts were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses broad keywords such as remove, generated, writing, text, editing, and reviewing, and implicit invocation is enabled, so it could be selected for unrelated writing or editing requests.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No instructions or files request persistent memory changes, background services, scheduled tasks, privilege escalation, credential access, or tool hijacking.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to help produce workflows, checklists, analysis, and related implementation support for humanizer-style productivity tasks; that is broad and somewhat vague, but the instructions stay within normal assistant output generation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Installers should be aware that the skill may activate too easily on ordinary writing or editing requests. Prefer explicit invocation by skill name, and consider narrowing its trigger keywords before relying on implicit routing.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The scanner's broad-trigger concern is supported by the artifact: the manifest, README files, reference plan, and agent YAML use generic triggers with implicit invocation. This is a routing and usability concern, but it is not paired with sensitive authority or unsafe runtime behavior.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The Chinese README contains substantial English text. That is a localization quality issue, not a security concern.
[AIG-SARIF] expected: The static scan reported no T01-T09 security findings, which matches inspection of the documentation-only artifact set.
